newsitem.title: USA: Peru rebels "implicity" roll back demand - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels "implicity" roll back demand - report.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in Lima had "implicity" agreed to drop their key demand and not seek the release of their jailed comrades, according to an interview in the Washington Post on Sunday.

Fujimori also said that the rebels, who have been holding the hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence for six weeks, agreed to work toward a solution "according to Peruvian law," the report said.

The statement could mark a major breakthrough in the stand-off that began on Dec. 17 when the rebels stormed a party at the residence, seized 500 hostages and demanded that their fellow Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) members in jail be freed.
"We convinced them they can't push the liberation of MRTA prisoners; it took a lot of time, but we were very patient," Fujimori said in the interview with the Post.
All recent statements by the MRTA have expressly called for talks to include their demand for the release of about 400 jailed comrades in return for the hostages.
As recently as Saturday, the MRTA rebel leading the operation in Lima, Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, said that he would release his captives only after all his jailed comrades were freed.
"We have come for one goal and we will not renounce it," Cerpa said from inside the residence in a walkie-talkie interview with the CBS Telenoticias network.
But in Washington, Fujimori told the Post in an interview that the rebels had agreed to drop their chief demand from a joint agenda for dialogue that has been under discussion.
"For us this is an advance," Fujimori was quoted as saying.
Fujimori flew to Washington on Saturday after an emergency summit on the crisis in Toronto with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
At the summit, Fujimori and Hashimoto agreed to push for direct talks with the rebels, even though they reiterated they would not consider the demand for the freedom of MRTA rebels in prison.
Before returning to Lima on Monday, Fujimori is scheduled to meet with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and other State Department officials to discuss the crisis.
The rebels originally took more than 500 hostages on Dec. 17 during a lavish cocktail party at the diplomatic mansion but have freed most of them.
The remaining 72 captives in the mined and booby-trapped residence include two Peruvian ministers, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, about two dozen Japanese businessmen and Fujimori's brother.
